---
title: "Why does spectroscopy measure a response?"
description: "Because every probe couples weakly to an operator of the sample, and what is detected is the induced change."
categories: [response]
order: 20
date: 2026-08-12
draft: true
---

::: {.oneline}
An experiment supplies a perturbation and records how the sample reacts. Provided the probe is weak, that reaction is linear in the drive, and the proportionality kernel is the response function — regardless of the apparatus.
:::

## Short answer

*To write.* An experiment supplies a perturbation and records how the sample reacts. Provided the probe is weak, that reaction is linear in the drive, and the proportionality kernel is the response function — regardless of the apparatus.
